q: 1. The property of fresh concrete, in which the water in the mix tends to rise to the surface while placing and compacting, is called ...........
explain: Bleeding is a form of segregation where water comes out to the surface of the concrete because it has the lowest specific gravity among the ingredients.

q: 2. Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete, is ...........
explain: In the absence of specific data, the design value for total shrinkage strain is taken as 0.0003 as per IS:456.

q: 3. Strength of concrete increases with ...........
explain: Finer cement provides more surface area for hydration, leading to a more rapid development of strength.

q: 4. Increase in the moisture content in concrete ...........
explain: Higher moisture content beyond the required water-cement ratio increases the volume of voids once evaporated, thus reducing strength.

q: 5. As compared to ordinary portland cement, high alumina cement has ...........
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial and final setting times
lower initial and final setting times
explain: High Alumina Cement (HAC) is characterized by a high initial setting time but a very rapid final setting and hardening process.

q: 6. A twisted bar has about ........... more yield stress than ordinary mild steel bar.
explain: Cold twisting increases the yield strength of the steel by approximately 50% due to the strain hardening effect.

q: 7. M 10 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: Standard nominal mix proportions for M10 concrete is 1 part cement, 3 parts fine aggregate, and 6 parts coarse aggregate.

q: 8. M 20 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: The nominal mix for M20 concrete is 1:1.5:3, providing a characteristic strength of 20 N/mm².

q: 9. The reason for choosing mild steel bars as reinforcement in tensile zones of concrete is that ...........
options: The modulus of elasticity of mild steel is about the same as that of concrete
The Poisson's ratio of mild steel is almost the same as that of concrete
The coefficient of linear expansion is about the same as that of concrete
The stress-strain plots of both mild steel and concrete are identical in shape
explain: Steel and concrete expand and contract at nearly the same rate with temperature changes, preventing internal bond failure.

q: 10. The shape of the stress-strain curve of concrete up to a strain of 0.002 is ...........
explain: The idealized stress-strain curve for concrete consists of a parabolic portion from zero strain to 0.002, followed by a rectangular portion up to 0.0035.

q: 11. The balanced design gives ...........
explain: A balanced section utilizes the full capacity of both materials simultaneously, resulting in the most compact concrete section for a given set of materials.

q: 12. The allowable tensile stress in mild steel stirrups in reinforced cement concrete is (in N/mm2) ...........
explain: For mild steel (Fe 250) used as shear reinforcement in WSM, the permissible tensile stress is 140 N/mm².

q: 13. If the factored moment to be carried by a rectangular section is more than the limiting moment of the section ...........
options: the section can be designed as a over-reinforced section
the section has to be redesigned increasing the dimensions or design the section as doubly reinforced
explain: Since over-reinforcement is forbidden, you must either increase the beam size or add compression steel (doubly reinforced) to carry the extra moment.

q: 14. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is ............
explain: The standard beam specimen for the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) test is $150 	imes 150 	imes 700$ mm.

q: 15. Normally, the tensile strength of concrete is about ............ of its compressive strength.
explain: Concrete is very weak in tension; its tensile strength is usually estimated at about 1/10th or 10-15% of its compressive strength.

q: 16. When the lever arm of a reinforced concrete beam is z and width of beam is b, then the maximum shear stress in a beam subjected to shear force F will be equal to ............
explain: Maximum shear stress in Working Stress Method is calculated as Shear Force / (Width x Lever Arm).

q: 17. When a reinforced concrete structure is loaded, the resistance first broken is
explain: The bond between steel and concrete is composed of adhesion, friction, and mechanical interlock. Adhesive resistance (the chemical bond) is the first to fail as soon as there is any microscopic slip.

q: 18. A doubly reinforced beam is considered less economical than a singly reinforced beam because
options: tensile steel requires is more than that for balanced section
concrete is not stressed to its full value
explain: In a doubly reinforced beam, the stress in the compression steel is limited by the strain in the surrounding concrete. Often, it does not reach its full yield strength, making the use of steel less efficient than in the tension zone.

q: 19. When the T-beam is continuous, the assumed overall depth of the beam of heavy loads is taken as
explain: Continuous beams under heavy loads require higher stiffness, leading to a depth assumption closer to 1/10 to 1/12 of the span.

q: 20. In a reinforced concrete T-beam (in which the flange is in compression), the position of neutral axis will
options: depend on the thickness of flange is in relation to total depth and percentage of reinforcement
at the junction of flange and web
explain: The position of the neutral axis is determined by the equilibrium of total compression and total tension, which depends on the steel ratio and the geometry of the section.

q: 21. The partial factor of safety for steel in limit state design is
explain: The partial safety factor for steel (γs) is 1.15 because steel is a factory-manufactured material with better quality control than concrete.

q: 22. In singly reinforced simply supported beams, the reinforced steel bars are placed
options: near the bottom of the beam
near the top of the beam
at the neutral axis of the beam
anywhere in the cross section of the beam
explain: In a simply supported beam, the bottom fiber is in tension, so the reinforcement must be placed there.

q: 23. The distance between the lines of action of compression and tensile forces in a singly reinforced beam is called
explain: The lever arm (z) is the internal distance between the resultant compressive force (C) in concrete and the resultant tensile force (T) in steel.

q: 24. The ratio of the limiting value of the depth of neutral axis and the depth of the section of a singly reinforced beam is equal to
explain: This formula is derived from the linear strain diagram where the maximum concrete strain is 0.0035 and the minimum steel strain is 0.002 + 0.87fy/Es.

q: 25. The most economical design of singly reinforced beams is given by
explain: Limit State Method (LSM) is more economical as it uses partial safety factors and accounts for the non-linear behavior of concrete, allowing for smaller sections than WSM.

q: 26. For a rectangular simply supported beam for 4.5 m effective span, based on the code restriction, the depth is
explain: For a simply supported beam, span/depth = 20. Thus, Depth = 4500 / 20 = 225 mm.

q: 27. In doubly reinforced beams, the percentage of the maximum compression reinforcement of the gross cross-sectional area of beam should not exceed
explain: Similar to tension reinforcement, compression reinforcement is also capped at 4% of the gross area to prevent congestion.

q: 28. For simply supported beams of spans above 10 m, span to depth ratio 20 must be multiplied to get permitted value by
explain: For spans exceeding 10m, the span-to-depth ratios are modified by multiplying by (10 / span in meters).

q: 29. For the design of flexural members, the safety partial fact for compressive strength
explain: The partial safety factor for concrete (γc) is 1.5.

q: 30. The maximum spacing of the torsional reinforcement in R.C.C. beams must not exceed
explain: Torsional stirrups must be closely spaced; the limit is the least of x1, (x1+y1)/4, or 300mm.

q: 31. The probability that the actual strengths of material is more than or equal to its characteristic strength is
explain: Characteristic strength is defined as the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall, meaning 95% are above it.

q: 32. In a prestressed member it is advisable to use
options: low strength concrete but high tensile steel
high strength concrete and high tensile steel
explain: High strength concrete is needed to resist high bearing stresses at anchorages and minimize creep/shrinkage losses, while high tensile steel is required to maintain effective prestress after accounting for various losses.

q: 33. Post tensioning system
options: was widely used in earlier days
is not economical and hence not generally used
is economical for large spans and is adopted now a days
explain: Post-tensioning allows for thinner slabs and longer spans without intermediate columns, making it highly economical for bridges and large commercial buildings today.

q: 34. The ultimate moment resisting capacity of a simple supported pre-stressed concreted beam is obtained by using
options: stress-strain relationship of concrete and steel
explain: The analysis of prestressed sections at the ultimate limit state requires satisfying both equilibrium of forces and the compatibility of strains between steel and concrete.

q: 35. For M 150 grade concrete (1 : 2 : 4) the moment of resistance factor is
explain: The Q factor (Moment of Resistance factor) for M15 grade concrete in WSM (balanced section) is approximately 8.5.

q: 36. An under-reinforced section means
options: steel is provided at the underside only
steel provided on one face only
explain: In an under-reinforced section, the steel reaches its yield stress before the concrete reaches its maximum compressive strain, providing ductile failure.
